skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-google-ads-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up Google Ads bidding on revenue or profit from paid repeat orders in WooCommerce. Verify tracking before you change a campaign goal.
skill.summary: Configure and verify Google Ads bidding on WooCommerce repeat orders through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are ordinary documentation or scoped business checks, with no evidence of system reconnaissance or prompt injection. Confirmed risks include unpinned installer execution, agent writes without a general confirmation gate, and order lookups without data minimization. The workflow also lacks safeguards for returned browser URLs, unrelated credentials, and the scope and timing of customer data transfers.

remediation.issue: Unpinned package runner and skill source in the install command.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and skill commit. Require user approval before downloading or executing the installer.

remediation.issue: Authenticated MCP calls and setup writes lack a general approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the connector and workspace. Limit tools to this workflow and require approval before each setup change or retry that affects live state.

remediation.issue: Recent-order checks can retrieve more data than classification requires.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the store scope and request only classification counts or the fields needed for a specific order check.

remediation.issue: The general WooCommerce guide can expand a Google Ads setup to unrelated ad channels.
remediation.suggestion: Identify Product Metrics and the destination account before connection. Limit setup to Google Ads and require separate approval for other destinations or audience features.

remediation.issue: The initial order import comes before the documented consent review.
remediation.suggestion: Before any import, disclose the history, fields, and recipients involved. Verify the merchant's permissions and applicable consent settings, then request explicit approval.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs use returned URLs without documented destination checks.
remediation.suggestion: Check the HTTPS host against an approved list for the current connection step. Show the verified destination and stop on unexpected hosts.

remediation.issue: The skill includes exceptions for unrelated credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Remove unrelated exceptions. Use the service's browser authorization flow or a protected secret input, and keep secrets out of chat and command arguments.

semantic_findings.title: Tracking Setup Can Expand Beyond Google Ads
semantic_findings.description: The skill selects Product Metrics even when the merchant does not name it. Its linked WooCommerce checklist directs the merchant to connect two unrelated ad channels without a Google-only step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback guide explicitly names Meta and ChatGPT Ads alongside Google Ads. Connection requires merchant action, so the risk is unintended scope expansion, not automatic disclosure.

semantic_findings.title: Initial Order Import Precedes Consent Review
semantic_findings.description: The WooCommerce guide queues an initial order import before its consent configuration step. The initial import step does not explain which customer fields or historical orders it sends to Product Metrics.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The step order is explicit. The documentation says consent controls ad conversion delivery, so this finding concerns vendor import before review, not a proven advertising consent bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Handoff Does Not Verify Destinations
semantic_findings.description: The assistant relays tool-provided browser URLs to the merchant without a documented scheme or host check. An unexpected link may appear to be part of authorized setup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff trusts the returned browser URL and specifies no destination check. No evidence found of a malicious URL, and the merchant must open the link.

semantic_findings.title: Unrelated Credentials May Reach Command Inputs
semantic_findings.description: The secrets rule permits requesting Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI credentials, none of which are needed for this setup. It directs the assistant to pass them to a command without specifying protected input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credential exceptions are explicit. The rule prohibits logging, but it does not prevent secret exposure through chat, tool traces, or process arguments.

content.user_title: Set Up Google Ads Bidding for WooCommerce Repeat Orders
content.value_statement: A retention campaign can optimize for first purchases when it uses the default purchase goal. Use Product Metrics to verify repeat-order signals and choose a revenue or profit goal.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status for the selected workspace and store.
Guide the merchant through connecting WooCommerce and Google Ads and configuring consent.
Check whether selected paid orders count as new, returning, or unknown.
Explain which Google Ads conversion action to use for repeat-order revenue or profit.
Guide repeat-order delivery tests and read back conversion action status after the merchant makes changes.
limitations: Live checks require authorized access to Product Metrics. The WooCommerce integration requires a Pro workspace.
The merchant handles WordPress and Google Ads actions and chooses the primary conversion goal.
Profit values require complete order costs and active additional cost settings.
This workflow does not configure acquisition, lifetime value bidding, or bidding on profit from all purchases.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Find which connection and tracking steps are still missing before setting up repeat-order bidding.

use_cases.title: Pilot a Retention Campaign
use_cases.description: Compare repeat-order revenue and profit goals, then plan a trial in one campaign without changing other campaigns.

use_cases.title: Validate Repeat-Order Tracking
use_cases.description: Check test order classification and delivery. Review paid statuses, cost completeness, and consent settings when the expected conversion is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my selected WooCommerce store and Google Ads account are ready for repeat-order bidding. List missing prerequisites without changing settings.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Test Order
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a second paid test order. Check its repeat classification and delivery without displaying customer identifiers or changing campaign settings.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Conversion Goal
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the repeat-order revenue and profit goals for my store. Check whether costs are complete and recommend a goal for one retention campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Campaign Pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review a campaign after a manual change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the goal I selected for my retention campaign. Verify its conversion action status and flag duplicate primary purchase actions. Report the bid strategy and target ROAS when available.

output_examples.input: Show an example of the result after checking a repeat test order.
output: The paid test order is classified as returning.
WooCommerce shows Live order delivery: Verified.
The revenue conversion action is ready. Check Google Ads for a recorded conversion before changing the campaign goal.

output_examples.input: Show an example recommendation when order costs are missing.
output: Use Product Metrics - Returning Customer for the trial because some order costs are missing.
Set the goal on one retention campaign and leave the other campaign goals unchanged.
Review conversion volume and cost coverage before switching to the profit action.

best_practices: Confirm the store, Google Ads client account, and permitted data destinations before enabling tracking.
Verify a second paid test order and confirm consent settings before changing the bidding goal.
Start with one campaign and avoid counting the same purchase under two primary actions.
anti_patterns: Pasting the WooCommerce setup token into a chat.
Choosing profit bidding while order costs are incomplete.
Changing account-wide goals when only one retention campaign needs a repeat-order goal.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. This workflow uses the Product Metrics WooCommerce plugin and a Pro workspace to supply conversion data.

faq.question: What counts as a returning customer?
faq.answer: A customer counts as returning when WooCommerce has an earlier order in a selected paid status. Guest orders match by billing email.

faq.question: What is the difference between the two conversion actions?
faq.answer: Returning Customer uses repeat-order revenue. Returning Customer Profit uses profit after product and additional costs.

faq.question: Can the assistant change the primary conversion goal?
faq.answer: No. The assistant can show the steps and verify the result. You choose and apply the goal in Google Ads.

faq.question: Do I need to remove my current purchase tracking?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics creates secondary actions. When you switch goals, make sure the campaign does not count the same purchase under two primary actions.

faq.question: What happens when a repeat order is refunded?
faq.answer: Product Metrics adjusts the corresponding Google Ads conversion when WooCommerce records a refund or cancellation.
